This site presents sea ice extent and thickness across regions off Alaska, aligned with Large Marine Ecosystems supported by AKFIN." Explore how sea ice changes over time, 
check recent conditions, and download data for further analysis.

## Sea Ice Extent

Sea ice extent measures how much ocean area is covered by ice, and how that 
coverage shifts across seasons and years. [Learn more and explore the data](extent.qmd).

## Sea Ice Thickness

Sea ice thickness reflects how the ice itself has changed over time, based on 
average conditions in October, March, and April. [Learn more and explore the data](sit.qmd).

## Large Marine Ecosystems

In federal fisheries management, the Alaska region is made up of distinct large marine 
ecosystems across the Gulf of Alaska (GOA), Aleutian Islands (AI), 
eastern Bering Sea (including the northern Bering Sea), and 
Chukchi and Beaufort Seas (referred to here as the Alaskan Arctic). 
Fishery management areas include the Gulf of Alaska and Bering Sea/Aleutian Islands. No federal fisheries currently occur in the Alaskan Arctic.
